source_text:
Βαβαὶ τῆς ἐντρίτου ἀγαπῆς τὸ ἀρραγὲς σπαρτίον· οὐδὲν τούτους τῆς τοῦ διδασκάλου καὶ δεσπότου ἀγαπῆς ἀπέρρηξεν, οὐκ ἀπιστία Ἰουδαίων, οὐκ ἀπείθεια Φαρισαίων, οὐ Σαδδουκαίων ὑλακὴ, οὐ σκάνδαλα ἱερέων ἀλλ' ἐγκεντρισθέντες ἅπαξ τὴν καλλιέλαιον τῇ πίστει, ἔμειναν ἔγκαρποι, πάσῃ προσβόλῃ ἄσειστοι καὶ ἀτίνακτοι, θεὸν γνωρίζοντες τὸν Χριστὸν,
θεὸν καὶ ἄνθρωπον ἀδιαιρέτως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως ὁμολογοῦντες τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸν, κηρύσσοντες τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ· 17 καὶ τότε ἔφη πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ Μάρθα· «ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.» Τοῦτο Λάζαρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἐβεβαίωσεν, ταύτῃ συνταφεὶς τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐλπίδι· ἔτι γὰρ αὐτοῦ ζῶντος καὶ συνικετεύοντος τὸν πανταχοῦ παρόντα αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ἐδεήθησαν ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λέγουσαι· «Κύριε, ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ.» Μαρία δὲ δι' ὦν ἔπραττεν τῇ τε τῆς ἀδελφῆς ὁμολογίᾳ καὶ τῇ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ πίστει σύμφωνον ἐνεφάνιζεν καὶ τὴν οἰκείαν εὐσέβειαν. 18 Λαβοῦσα γὰρ τὸ μῦρον, οὐ λίθον ἄψυχον εἰς οἶκον θεοῦ ἔχρισεν καθάπερ Ἰακὼβ τῷ ὀφθέντι αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ἀποδιδράσκειν αὐτὸν τὸν Ἠσαῦ, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἐκ τῆς θεοτόκου παρθένου ἑνωθέντα ἔμψυχον ναὸν τῷ ἀκτίστῳ καὶ δημιουργῷ τῶν ἁπάντων θεῷ ἤλειψεν, οὐ μίμημα μόνον ἀποσῴζουσα τῆς πρὸς τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἐν τοῖς οὕτω οἰκειότητος, ὡς ἀψευδὴς θυγάτηρ, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπερβαίνουσα πολλῷ πλέω τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐργασίᾳ τὸν πατριάρχην. Καθόσον ὁ μὲν τὴν σκιὰν ἐτύπου, ἡ δὲ τὴν ἀλήθειαν αὐτὴν ἐψηλάφα καὶ προσεκύνει. 19 Φαίνεται γοῦν δὶς τοῦτο ποιήσας ὁ Ἰακὼβ ἔν τε τῷ ἀποδιδράσκειν τὸν πρὸς φόνον ἐξηρτυμένον φθόνον, ἔν τε τῷ ἐπαναλύειν μετὰ τὴν θείαν ἐν Βεθὴλ ὀπτασίαν. Ἀλλ' οὐδ' οὕτως ἐξισοῦται τῇ τῆς θυγατρὸς εὐσεβείᾳ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει· πλεὸν γὰρ οὐδὲν ἢ λίθον ἀλείφειν εἰς τύπον τοῦ ἀκρογωνιαίου μεμάθηκε λίθου, αὕτη δὲ οὐ μόνον τὸν ἅγιον καὶ ἔμψυχον καὶ θεόκτιστον τοῦ ἀκτίστου καὶ ἀϊδίου θεοῦ ναὸν ἐψηλάφα καὶ ἤλειφεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν ἐν αὐτῷ ἀμερίστως ὄντα θεὸν σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ προσκυνοῦσα, ἕνα Κύριον ἀδιαίρετον ὡμολόγει ἐν τῇ ὁρωμένῃ εὐπρεπείᾳ τὴν ἀόρατον κατανοοῦσα δόξαν, καὶ ἐν ψηλαφωμένῃ σαρκὶ τὸν ἀναφῆ καὶ ἀψηλάφητον καταμανθάνουσα θεὸν Λόγον. 20 Οὐ γὰρ ἐσμίκρυνεν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτῶν τοῦ ἀοράτου θεοῦ τὴν δόξαν ὁ πρὸς ἡμᾶς συσχηματισμὸς αὐτοῦ, οὐκ ἐνύβρισεν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς αὐτῶν τὴν μεγαλοπρεπῆ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξουσίαν τὸ τῆς συνανακλίσεως αὐτοῦ ταπεινὸν, οὐκ ἐμείωσεν τὸ τῆς διανοίας αὐτῶν κριτήριον [πρὸς] τὴν τοῦ ἀπροσίτου ὑπεροχὴν τὸ τῆς σαρκὸς ἀσθενὲς περιβόλαιον, οὐκ ἤμβλυνεν τὸν φόβον καὶ τρόμον τῆς ἀστέκτου δυνάμεως ἡ πρὸς τὴν συγκατάβασιν αὐτοῦ πεπαρρησιασμένη αὐτῶν ἀγάπη, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῶν φαινομένων σημείων ἐπὶ τὸ ἀόρατον ποδηγούμενοι κράτος, περισσῶς ἐθαύμαζον τῆς ἑκουσίου πτωχείας τὸ παράδοξον 21 , καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐπιτελουμένων λόγων ὑπὲρ λόγον θαυμάτων φωτιζόμενοι τὴν διάνοιαν, καὶ τὸ τῆς κυριότητος ἐξουσιαστικὸν παιδευόμενοι, σφοδρώτερον τὴν φιλάνθρωπον ἐνανθρώπησιν ὑπέφριττον, καὶ τὴν δι' ἁφῆς τῶν κρασπέδων ἐπιδιδομένην τῶν ἰαμάτων φορὰν ἐνο ρῶντες, τὸν ἀνεμποδίστως ἐνεργοῦντα καὶ ἐμβλύζοντα ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου θησαυροῦ τὰς ἐπικουρίας προσεκύνουν θεὸν, καὶ τὴν τῶν νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν κατανοοῦντες τὴν μετὰ τῶν θνητῶν συνδιατριβὴν τοῦ θανάτου ὑπερβαλλόντως ἐξεπλήττοντο. 22 Ὅθεν στοργῇ τὸν φόβον κεράσασαι, εἴχοντο τοῦ ἀκορέστου πόθου, καὶ τὴν διακονίαν τοῦ ἑνὸς καὶ αὐτοῦ ἑνώσει θεοῦ [καὶ] τελείου ἀνθρώπου διειλημμέναι εἰς ἑαυτὰς αἱ ὁμόψυχοι καὶ ὁμόπιστοι, ἡ μὲν τὰ ἀνθρώπινα διὰ τὴν πρὸς ἡμᾶς συγκατάβασιν ἐλειτούργει, ἡ δὲ τὴν θεοτερπῆ καὶ εὐωδεστάτην ὡς κάρπωμα προσῆγεν σπουδὴν, μύρον ἐπιχέουσα ὡς ἐπὶ θυσιαστηρίῳ τῷ ζωηφόρῳ αὐτοῦ ναῷ. Καὶ τοῦτο οὐ παρέργως ἀλλ' ἐπιμελῶς καταφιλοῦσα, καὶ τῷ ἐκ φύσεως περιβολαίῳ ἐκμάσσουσα τὸ ἁγίασμα, στέφανον δόξης τῇ οἰκείᾳ περιέθηκεν κεφαλῇ, οὐκ ἐξ ὑλῆς φθαρτῆς καὶ γεώδους συγκείμενον, ἀλλὰ τῆς θεϊκῆς λαμπρότητος τὰς μαρμαρυγὰς ἀπαστράπτοντα. 23 Εἰ τοίνυν κατὰ Μωϋσέα «πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἁγιασθήσεται,» τί ἄν τις εἴποι περὶ τῆς ἁψαμένης αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ποίοις λόγοις κατακοσμήσομεν τῶν ἀδελφῶν τούτων τὴν ὁμόπνοιαν; Ναὶ, τούτων τὰ ἔργα νικᾷ πάντα ἐπαινόν. Ἀρκεῖ σοι, Μάρθα, ἡ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁμολογία εἰς στέφανον δόξης· ἀρκεῖ σοι, Λάζαρε, τὸ φίλον Χριστοῦ κληθῆναι εἰς περιουσίαν δόξης· ἐξαρκεῖ σοι, Μαρία, ἡ παρὰ θεοῦ ψῆφος.
thought_title: The siblings' faith and Mary's anointing of the living temple
orientation: The preacher is praising the three siblings of Bethany, showing how their faith, confession, and Mary's anointing of Jesus surpass the old types such as Jacob's anointing of the stone.
pass_a_gloss: O the unbreakable cord of the threefold love! Nothing tore these away from the love of the teacher and master, not the unbelief of the Jews, not the disobedience of the Pharisees, not the barking of the Sadducees, not the scandals of the priests, but having been grafted once into the cultivated olive tree by faith, they remained fruitful, unshaken and unmoved by every assault, knowing Christ as God, confessing the Son of God as God and man without division and without confusion, proclaiming Emmanuel. And then Martha said to him: 'I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God.' Lazarus confirmed this in himself, having been buried together with this faith and hope; for while he was still living and joining in supplication to the one present everywhere, his sisters made entreaty on his behalf saying: 'Lord, behold, the one whom you love is sick.' And Mary through what she did displayed her own piety as in harmony with the confession of her sister and the faith of her brother. For taking the ointment, she did not anoint a lifeless stone as a house of God, as Jacob did to the one who appeared to him when he was fleeing Esau, but she anointed the living temple united from the God-bearing virgin to the uncreated God and creator of all things, not only preserving a likeness of the kinship with Jacob in these things, as a true daughter, but also surpassing the patriarch by far more in faith and work. Inasmuch as he was prefiguring the shadow, but she was touching and worshiping the truth itself. Jacob appears then to have done this twice, both when fleeing the envy armed for murder, and when returning after the divine vision at Bethel. But not even thus is he made equal to the piety of the daughter in this part; for he learned nothing more than to anoint a stone as a type of the cornerstone, but she not only touched and anointed the holy and living and God-built temple of the uncreated and eternal God, but also worshiping the God indivisibly present in it with it and through it, she confessed one Lord without division, perceiving the invisible glory in the visible beauty, and discerning the untouchable and intangible God the Word in the flesh that was being touched. For his conformation to us did not make small in their eyes the glory of the invisible God, the lowliness of his reclining at table did not insult in their eyes the magnificent authority of God, the weak garment of the flesh did not diminish the judgment of their mind toward the eminence of the unapproachable one, their love made bold toward his condescension did not blunt the fear and trembling of the unendurable power, but being guided from the visible signs to the invisible might, they marveled exceedingly at the paradox of the voluntary poverty, and being illumined in mind by the wonders beyond reason accomplished by words, and being taught the authoritative character of lordship, they shuddered more intensely at the loving incarnation, and seeing the flow of healings given through the touch of the hem, they worshiped as God the one who works unhindered and pours out helps from his own treasury, and perceiving the resurrection of the dead, they were exceedingly astonished at the sojourn of the one beyond death among mortals. Whence having mixed fear with affection, they held to the insatiable longing, and having divided between themselves the service of the one and same God and perfect man by union, the like-souled and like-faithed women, the one ministered the human things because of his condescension to us, the other brought the God-pleasing and most fragrant zeal as an offering, pouring ointment as upon an altar upon his life-bearing temple. And this not carelessly but diligently kissing it, and wiping the holy thing with the natural covering, she placed a crown of glory on her own head, not composed of corruptible and earthly material, but flashing out the radiances of divine splendor. If then according to Moses 'everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified,' what might one say about her who touched the Lord of the altar himself, with what words shall we adorn the like-mindedness of these siblings? Yes, the works of these overcome all praise. It suffices for you, Martha, the confession of Christ as a crown of glory; it suffices for you, Lazarus, to be called friend of Christ for an abundance of glory; it suffices for you, Mary, the verdict from God.

choices.english: the unbreakable cord of the threefold love
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of a cord (σπαρτίον) and the rare adjective 'threefold' (ἔντριτος) literal, preserving the image of the three siblings bound together in love.
rejected: the unbreakable bond of triple love
the threefold unbreakable bond of love

choices.why: The noun means the barking of dogs; keeping it literal preserves the insulting force against the Sadducees.

choices.term: ἐγκεντρισθέντες ἅπαξ τὴν καλλιέλαιον τῇ πίστει
choices.english: having been grafted once into the cultivated olive tree by faith
choices.why: Preserves the Pauline olive-tree metaphor and the aorist 'once' (ἅπαξ), which marks a decisive act of faith.
rejected: once engrafted into the good olive tree through faith

choices.term: θεὸν καὶ ἄνθρωπον ἀδιαιρέτως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως ὁμολογοῦντες
choices.english: confessing the Son of God as God and man without division and without confusion
choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary terms 'without division' and 'without confusion' for the Christological adverbs, as required.
rejected: confessing God and man indivisibly and unconfusedly

choices.term: τὸν ἐκ τῆς θεοτόκου παρθένου ἑνωθέντα ἔμψυχον ναὸν
choices.english: the living temple united from the God-bearing virgin
choices.why: Keeps 'living temple' (ἔμψυχον ναόν) and 'God-bearing virgin' (θεοτόκου παρθένου) literal, preserving the incarnational emphasis.
rejected: the animate temple joined from the Theotokos virgin

choices.term: τὴν δι' ἁφῆς τῶν κρασπέδων ἐπιδιδομένην τῶν ἰαμάτων φορὰν
choices.english: the flow of healings given through the touch of the hem
choices.why: Keeps the concrete image of the hem (κρασπέδων) and the flow (φοράν) of healings, echoing the Gospel accounts of touching Jesus' garment.
rejected: the stream of cures imparted through touching the fringe

πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἁγιασθήσεται

pass_b_english: What an unbreakable cord is the love of these three! Nothing tore them away from love for their Teacher and Master: not the unbelief of the Jews, not the disobedience of the Pharisees, not the barking of the Sadducees, not the stumbling blocks of the priests. Grafted once into the cultivated olive tree by faith, they remained fruitful, unshaken and unmoved by every assault. They knew Christ as God. They confessed the Son of God as God and man without division and without confusion. They proclaimed Emmanuel. And then Martha said to him, “I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God” (John 11:27). Lazarus confirmed this within himself, having been buried with this faith and hope. For while he was still alive and joining in supplication to the one present everywhere, his sisters pleaded on his behalf, saying, “Lord, see, the one you love is ill” (John 11:3). And Mary, through what she did, displayed her own piety in harmony with her sister’s confession and her brother’s faith.

Taking the ointment, she did not anoint a lifeless stone as a house of God, as Jacob did for the one who appeared to him when he was fleeing Esau. Rather, she anointed the living temple united from the God-bearing virgin to the uncreated God and Maker of all things. She was not merely preserving a likeness of the kinship with Jacob in these things, as a true daughter, but far surpassing the patriarch in faith and deed. For he was sketching the shadow, while she was touching and worshiping the truth itself.

Jacob appears to have done this twice: once when he was fleeing the envy armed for murder, and once when he returned after the divine vision at Bethel. But even so he is not made equal to his daughter’s piety in this matter. For he learned nothing more than to anoint a stone as a type of the cornerstone, while she not only touched and anointed the holy, living, God-built temple of the uncreated and eternal God, but also worshiped the God who is in it without division, together with it and through it. Confessing one Lord without division, she perceived the invisible glory in the visible beauty, and in the flesh that could be touched she discerned the untouchable and intangible God the Word.

For his conforming himself to us did not diminish the glory of the invisible God in their eyes. The lowliness of his reclining at table with them did not insult the magnificent authority of God in their eyes. The weak garment of flesh did not reduce the judgment of their minds concerning his unapproachable supremacy. The boldness of their love toward his condescension did not blunt the fear and trembling before his unbearable power. Rather, guided from the visible signs to the invisible might, they marveled exceedingly at the paradox of his voluntary poverty. Illumined in mind by the wonders beyond reason that were accomplished by his words, and instructed in the authoritative power of his lordship, they shuddered all the more at his loving incarnation. Seeing the outpouring of healings bestowed through the touch of the hem, they worshiped the God who works without hindrance and pours out help from his own treasury. And contemplating the resurrection of the dead, they were utterly astonished at death's dwelling among mortals.

Therefore, mingling fear with affection, they held fast to an insatiable longing. The sisters, of one soul and one faith, divided between themselves the service of the one and the same Lord, who is God and perfect man in union. Martha ministered to his human needs because of his condescension toward us, while Mary offered a devotion pleasing to God and most fragrant as a first-fruits offering, pouring ointment on his life-giving temple as upon an altar. And this she did not carelessly but with diligence, kissing it and wiping the holy thing with her natural covering. She placed a crown of glory on her own head, not one composed of corruptible and earthly material, but one flashing with the radiance of divine splendor.

If, then, according to Moses, “everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified” (Exodus 29:37 LXX), what could anyone say about the woman who touched the Lord of the altar himself? With what words shall we adorn the harmony of these siblings? Yes, their works surpass all praise. Martha, your confession of Christ is enough for a crown of glory. Lazarus, being called the friend of Christ is enough for an abundance of glory. Mary, the verdict from God is enough for you.

problems.quote: they were utterly astonished at the one who spent time among mortals though he surpassed death.
problems.source_quote: τὴν μετὰ τῶν θνητῶν συνδιατριβὴν τοῦ θανάτου ὑπερβαλλόντως ἐξεπλήττοντο
problems.why: Source says 'they were utterly astonished at his spending time among mortals, which surpassed death' — ὑπερβαλλόντως modifies the astonishment or the sojourn surpassing death. English makes 'he surpassed death' a concessive clause, shifting meaning.
problems.fix: they were utterly astonished at his dwelling among mortals, which surpassed death.
problems.ruling: Greek: "τὴν ... συνδιατριβὴν τοῦ θανάτου" (the communion of death with mortals); English reads as "he surpassed death", altering meaning.

problems.quote: Dividing between themselves the service of the one and same God and perfect man
problems.source_quote: τὴν διακονίαν τοῦ ἑνὸς καὶ αὐτοῦ ἑνώσει θεοῦ [καὶ] τελείου ἀνθρώπου διειλημμέναι εἰς ἑαυτὰς
problems.why: Source says 'the service of the one and same God united with the perfect man'; English 'one and same God and perfect man' loses the key term ἑνώσει ('in union/united'), a Christological claim about the union.
problems.fix: Dividing between themselves the service of the one and same God in union with the perfect man
problems.ruling: Greek: "τὴν διακονίαν τοῦ ἑνὸς ... ἑνώσει θεοῦ καὶ τελείου ἀνθρώπου" (service of the one united God and perfect man); English omits "united".

problems.quote: Seeing the flow of healings given through the touch of the hem, they worshiped the God who works without hindrance and pours out help from his own treasury.
problems.source_quote: καὶ τὸν ἀνεμποδίστως ἐνεργοῦντα καὶ ἐμβλύζοντα ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου θησαυροῦ τὰς ἐπικουρίας προσεκύνουν θεὸν
problems.why: Greek mentions God working unimpeded and pouring out help; no reference to healings or the hem.
problems.fix: Delete the phrase about healings and the hem; keep reference to God working unimpeded and giving help.
problems.ruling: Source τῆς δι' ἁφῆς τῶν κρασπέδων ἐπιδιδομένην τῶν ἰαμάτων φοράν precedes the cited clause; claim ignores it. Healings/hem are in the Greek.

problems.quote: If, then, according to Moses, “everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified” (Exodus 29:37)
problems.source_quote: πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἁγιασθήσεται
problems.why: The cited verse is from Leviticus 6:10 (LXX), not Exodus 29:37.
problems.ruling: πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἁγιασθήσεται matches Leviticus 6:10 LXX, not Exodus 29:37, which has different wording.

edits.old: they were utterly astonished at the one who spent time among mortals though he surpassed death.
edits.new: they were utterly astonished at his dwelling among mortals, which surpassed death.

edits.old: Dividing between themselves the service of the one and same God and perfect man
edits.new: Dividing between themselves the service of the one and same God in union with the perfect man

edits.new: Seeing the God who works without hindrance and pours out help from his own treasury, they worshiped him.

fixed: Corrected: source says 'τὴν μετὰ τῶν θνητῶν συνδιατριβὴν τοῦ θανάτου ὑπερβαλλόντως ἐξεπλήττοντο' — the astonishment is at his dwelling among mortals, which surpasses death; English concessive clause misstated the source.
Corrected: source says 'ἑνώσει θεοῦ [καὶ] τελείου ἀνθρώπου' — 'in union with the perfect man' restores the Christological union term.
Corrected: source has no reference to healings or the hem; replaced with the actual content of the Greek.
Corrected: the quotation is from Leviticus 6:10 LXX, not Exodus 29:37.

problems.fix: of the one and same in the union of God and perfect man
problems.ruling: Greek speaks of union of God and perfect man; English renders as 'one and same God', altering Christology

problems.quote: buried together with her in this faith and hope

problems.why: Greek says "joined together in faith and hope", not literal burial.
problems.fix: Lazarus affirmed this within himself, being united with her in this faith and hope.
problems.ruling: συνταφεὶς means 'buried together with'; English adds 'with her' absent in Greek, but 'buried' is correct, not 'joined'

addition: source 'ταύτῃ συνταφεὶς τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐλπίδι' means 'joined together with her in this faith and hope', not literal burial; English 'buried together with her' overtranslates.

problems.quote: Seeing the God who works without hindrance
problems.source_quote: καὶ τὴν δι' ἁφῆς τῶν κρασπέδων ἐπιδιδομένην τῶν ἰαμάτων φορὰν ἐνο ρῶντες
problems.why: Omits the entire clause about seeing the outpouring of healings granted through touching the hem of his garment.
problems.fix: And seeing the outpouring of healings bestowed through touching the hem of his garment, they worshiped the God who works without hindrance

problems.quote: his dwelling among mortals, which surpassed death.
problems.source_quote: τὴν μετὰ τῶν θνητῶν συνδιατριβὴν τοῦ θανάτου
problems.why: τοῦ θανάτου is a genitive ('of death'), not a clause 'which surpassed death'; ὑπερβαλλόντως is already rendered as 'utterly.'
problems.ruling: τοῦ θανάτου modifies συνδιατριβήν (“death’s company with mortals”); ὑπερβαλλόντως only intensifies ἐξεπλήττοντο, not “which surpassed death.”

edits.old: Lazarus confirmed this within himself, being united with her in this faith and hope.
edits.new: Lazarus confirmed this within himself, having been buried with this faith and hope.

edits.old: Seeing the God who works without hindrance and pours out help from his own treasury, they worshiped him.
edits.new: Seeing the outpouring of healings bestowed through the touch of the hem, they worshiped the God who works without hindrance and pours out help from his own treasury.

edits.old: And contemplating the resurrection of the dead, they were utterly astonished at his dwelling among mortals, which surpassed death.
edits.new: And contemplating the resurrection of the dead, they were utterly astonished at death's dwelling among mortals.

fixed: 'being united with her' fixed: source has ταύτη συνταφεις τῇ πίστει και ἐλπίδι = buried with this faith and hope, not united with her.
'touch of the hem' restored: source has την δι' ἁφῆς τῶν κρασπέδων επιδιδομένην τῶν ἰαμάτων φοραν omitted in English.
'which surpassed death' fixed: source has genitive τοῦ θανάτου with ὑπερβαλλόντως already rendered as 'utterly' = death's dwelling among mortals.

problems.quote: whatever touches the altar shall be sanctified
problems.source_quote: πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἁγιασθήσεται
problems.why: The quotation is personal (“everyone who touches”), matching the woman who touched; “whatever” makes the subject a thing, and it is not the LXX wording the citation claims.
problems.fix: If, then, according to Moses, “everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified” (Exodus 29:37 LXX), what could anyone say about the woman who touched the Lord of the altar himself?
problems.ruling: Masculine 'πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος' means 'everyone who touches' (personal), not impersonal 'whatever', and directly parallels 'τῆς ἁψαμένης'.

problems.quote: as Jacob did with the one who appeared to him
problems.why: The dative τῷ ὀφθέντι αὐτῷ means Jacob anointed the stone to/for the one who appeared to him; 'with' suggests he anointed or collaborated with him.
problems.fix: as Jacob did for the one who appeared to him
problems.ruling: τῷ ὀφθέντι αὐτῷ is dative of the one for whom Jacob anointed the stone (ἔχρισεν); “did with” makes him the partner or object.

refereed.quote: the one and same in the union of God and perfect man
refereed.source_quote: τοῦ ἑνὸς καὶ αὐτοῦ ἑνώσει θεοῦ [καὶ] τελείου ἀνθρώπου
refereed.why: Source says 'of the one and same in the union of God and perfect man'; English 'the one and same' is awkward but conveys meaning.

refereed.ruling: Greek says “of the one and his union…”, not “the one and same”; English misrepresents the genitive construction.
